svg.title: Use intermediate products to test enzyme explanations
svg.desc: Three qualitative evidence patterns compare open templates with absent starts, completed fragments with unsealed junctions, and more mismatches in a proofreading-deficient model. They suggest different hypotheses about initiation, joining or accuracy but require controls for alternative polymerase, substrate and assay problems. Ligase requires suitable adjacent ends; it does not fill an arbitrary missing DNA interval. Reduced proofreading can raise mismatch frequency without independently establishing a lasting mutation or an organism-level effect, because repair and subsequent copying matter. Measurements of amount, accuracy and function remain distinct. No quantitative experiment is invented.

g.text: Use intermediate products to test enzyme explanations
A low overall yield can arise through different mechanisms.
Open templates; few or no new starts
A primer/start problem is possible. Also test polymerase, substrates and assay function.
Strand separation alone does not establish successful synthesis.
A joining problem is possible if adjacent ends and replacement DNA are suitable.
Ligase seals a backbone nick; it cannot supply a missing long sequence.
More mismatches in a proofreading-deficient model
Supports lower accuracy under the tested conditions; repair and later copying still matter.
A mismatch count alone does not identify protein function or an organism-level phenotype.
Compare reference and altered conditions with the same method; identify the measured intermediate.
DNA yield, copying accuracy and functional outcomes are different measurements.
